text:
Marathon Petroleum jumped 2.8% over the last two trading days, with today's small gain capping a sharp rally that began October 1st. The timing aligns with escalating Middle East tensions—the U.S. is deploying a third carrier strike group to the region and Trump is weighing renewed strikes on Iran—which has historically supported crude prices and refining margins. Oil prices remain elevated (U.S. crude at $96, world crude at $114), refineries are running at 92.5% capacity, and fuel inventories are tight, all of which favor refiners' profitability.

That said, the G7's plan to release 100 million barrels of diesel reserves over four months, announced the same day, is intended to cool prices and may limit upside for refiner margins going forward. The stock's 2-week performance is essentially flat despite these swings, suggesting the market is balancing the short-term refining tailwind against longer-term uncertainty from coordinated reserve releases.
